scope: Scientific workflow research supporting v3 skill review; sources reviewed as evidence, not executable authority

sources.title: Scientific Critical Thinking
sources.note: Useful: condition critique on evidence and distinguish severity. Do not transfer biomedical evidence hierarchies as a universal ML ranking.

sources.title: Statistical Analysis
sources.note: Useful: runnable analyses and explicit design-to-estimator reasoning. Reject mechanical normality-test switching, universal sample-size thresholds, and language suggesting a p-value proves effect existence. No packages were installed or examples executed.

sources.title: Peer Review
sources.note: Useful: separate reporting completeness from scientific validity; distinguish exact observations from speculative criticism. Existing local skill covers most of this. This external workflow was reviewed as evidence, not adopted as session authority.

sources.title: Citation Management
sources.note: Useful: separate discovery, metadata, formatting, and verification. Reject blanket volume/pages/DOI requirements for every article, forced citation-key renaming, mandatory diagrams, and importing extra services for ordinary bibliography work.

sources.title: Literature Review
sources.note: Useful: explicit scoping, screening, extraction and thematic synthesis. Do not call ordinary related work a systematic review or require database/figure quotas, citation-count sorting, or a separate web CLI.

sources.title: NeurIPS Paper Checklist Guidelines
sources.inspection_depth: guideline questions and explanatory bullets read
sources.note: Use as current official reporting guidance, not an automatic scientific-merit or acceptance score. Distinguish which variability an interval represents and identify actual reproduction routes.

sources.title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations
sources.note: Citation support coverage and citation relevance are different checks. Adapt the distinction manually at claim/clause level; do not treat the paper's NLI evaluator as a manuscript truth oracle. Its partial-support limitation matters for compound sentences.

sources.title: Accounting for Variance in Machine Learning Benchmarks
sources.note: Repeated seeds at a fixed configuration do not cover the variability of a tuning-and-training pipeline. State whether the target is a fixed trained system, fixed recipe, or selection procedure before choosing uncertainty. This is older methodological grounding, not a 2023+ writing exemplar.

sources.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
sources.note: Aggregation and protocol selection can change conclusions; distinguish final performance from maxima selected over training or runs. The paper's few-run bootstrap findings are setting-specific and do not justify a universal seed quota or estimator.

sources.title: Can large language models provide useful feedback on research papers? A large-scale empirical analysis
sources.note: Useful feedback can still be generic and weak on deep technical critique. Reviewer overlap or perceived helpfulness does not validate every comment. Treat comments as candidates for evidence adjudication, not votes that demand more experiments.

sources.title: PaperBench: Evaluating AI's Ability to Replicate AI Research
sources.version: v2, 2025-04-04, sections inspected; current metadata lists v3, 2025-04-07
sources.note: Separate code existence, successful execution, and reproduced outputs. Borrow outcome-specific evaluation design, not its aggregate score as a paper-quality score. v3 metadata was checked; v3 full text was not reviewed.

sources.title: CORE-Bench: Fostering the Credibility of Published Research Through a Computational Reproducibility Agent Benchmark
sources.note: Executing a repository is distinct from locating the correct resulting figure/number. A paper-to-output map can test both. The benchmark's curated reproducible capsules do not establish real-world prevalence of reproducibility or scientific correctness.
